title: Approval-rate summary
headline: [[$11.7K]] lost to excess declines across three issues (0.29% of $4.0M processed). Two are still ongoing and cost [[$6.0K a week]] (1.3% of weekly volume). Approval rate [[fell to 83.3%]] in the last 7 days from 84.2% over the prior 53 days.

issues.name: DE Visa on ACQ_B
issues.paragraph: [[$4.7K]] lost since 12 Nov, [[35.3%]] of this segment's $13.4K volume. German Visa cards on ACQ_B decline at [[51.9%]] vs 17.2% normally (208 transactions), [[56.2%]] in the last 3 days. Codes 91 (0.3% to 23.1% of transactions) and 96 (0.7% to 12.5%) point to an ACQ_B connectivity or switch problem; no other country, brand or route shows a code 91 jump.

issues.name: FR merchant M003
issues.paragraph: [[$3.8K]] lost since 29 Oct, [[29.9%]] of this segment's $12.8K volume. Gaming merchant M003 declines [[47.8%]] of French cards vs 17.9% normally, across all brands and routes, still [[46.7%]] in the last 3 days. 3DS challenge failures jumped from 5.0% to 36.6% of transactions and no other merchant shows this, so M003's 3DS challenge setup is the likely cause.

issues.name: BR Mastercard
issues.paragraph: [[$3.2K]] lost from 11 to 24 Oct, [[9.2%]] of this segment's $34.6K volume. Brazilian Mastercard declines rose to [[24.0%]] vs 14.2% normally, across all merchants and mainly on ACQ_A and ACQ_B, and fell back after 24 Oct (8.1% in the last 3 days). Code 51 rose from 5.0% to 15.2% of transactions and roughly doubled on all three routes, pointing to an issuer-side change rather than our routing.

next_steps.what: German Visa traffic rerouted off ACQ_B (completed 19 Nov); follow-up with ACQ_B on the code 91/96 spike
deep-dive analysis of M003's 3DS challenge failures (due 19 Nov); call with the merchant
alert on the BR code 51 rate added (19 Nov); follow-up with Mastercard and BR issuers
